important.name: Named-target guard accepts directory runs it exists to forbid
important.summary:
test_every_fenced_test_run_names_its_target treats any token containing a slash as a named target (_NAMED_TARGET first alternative \S+(?:/|\\)\S+). A fenced run against a directory (`pytest tests/unit`, `npm test src/components`) or a bare run with any path-valued flag (`pytest -q --junitxml=out/report.xml`) passes, although the skill rule the test pins is 'name files or node ids, never a directory'. The guard therefore cannot catch a port that drifts to a directory-scoped run.

Also (tests): _TEST_COMMAND (line 21) matches only npm test, pytest, python -m pytest, cargo test and go test, and only at the start of a stripped fenced line or after '$ '. A port that drifts back to a bare 'npx jest', 'yarn test', 'pnpm test', 'uv run pytest' or 'python -m unittest' in a fence, or to a bare `pytest` in inline prose, passes test_every_fenced_test_run_names_its_target. The module docstring (lines 3-5) says the test catches 'a verification step that runs the whole suite bare', which holds only for those five spellings.

Also (system_shape): The module docstring and the skill rule (SKILL.md:199, 'never a directory') say a fenced run must name a file or node id. _NAMED_TARGET's first alternative, `\S+(?:/|\\)\S+`, matches any path with a slash in it, so a fenced `pytest tests/skills` or `npm test src/components` counts as named. test_every_fenced_test_run_names_its_target therefore cannot fail on the folder run the skill forbids. It catches only a fully bare command.

Also (roast): `_NAMED_TARGET` accepts any `\S+/\S+` token, so a fenced `pytest tests/unit` or `npm test src/components` counts as a named target. The skill's rule (SKILL.md:199) is "name files or node ids, never a directory", and this is the test meant to keep the port from drifting back to directory runs. As written it only catches a run with no argument at all, which is the easy case.

Also (roast): writing-good-tests.md:47-52 and :193 list "greps source text, or asserts a removed symbol stays removed" as a warning sign, and say agent-instructing documents are tested by behavior (`harness:strap-skills`). The same PR ships `"superpowers" not in text` and `"human partner" not in text.lower()` (test_tdd_strapped_skill_contract.py:46-49), plus the strap-debugging route checks, which do exactly that. The project accepts contract tests as a strap part, but the reference reads as if they are always wrong. A reader who follows the reference would delete these tests.

Attack: Add a fenced block to plugins/harness/skills/tdd-strapped/SKILL.md containing the line `pytest tests/unit` (or `npm test src/components`, or `pytest -q --junitxml=out/report.xml`), then run `python -m pytest tests/skills/test_tdd_strapped_skill_contract.py -q`: it still passes. Probe (docs/_scratch/pr_review/0337/pr337_20261124T062651Z/probes/probe_regex.py) shows _TEST_COMMAND matches and _NAMED_TARGET matches for all three lines, so flagged_bare=False.
fix: Tighten _NAMED_TARGET to require a file-shaped token or a node id, e.g. r"(?:^|\s)[^\s-]\S*\.(?:py|ts|js|rs|go)(?:::\S+)?\b|::" so a bare path segment without a file extension no longer counts, and ignore tokens starting with '-'.

Add a negative self-check in the test module asserting that _NAMED_TARGET rejects 'pytest tests/unit' and 'pytest -q --junitxml=out/report.xml' and accepts 'npm test src/form.test.ts' and 'pytest tests/x.py::test_a'.
Widen _TEST_COMMAND to the common runners (npx jest|npx vitest|yarn test|pnpm test|uv run pytest|python -m unittest) and allow any leading prefix such as 'Run: '.
Narrow the module docstring to say the guard covers the runner spellings the skill uses today.
Drop the slash alternative: `_NAMED_TARGET = re.compile(r"\S+\.(?:py|ts|js|rs|go)\b|::")`. Every current fenced run (`npm test path/to/test.test.ts`, `npm test src/form.test.ts`) still matches.
Require a file extension or a node id: `_NAMED_TARGET = re.compile(r"\S+\.(?:py|ts|js|rs|go)\b|::")`. Both fenced runs in SKILL.md (`path/to/test.test.ts`, `src/form.test.ts`) still match.

Add one line to writing-good-tests.md's "Behavior, not text" paragraph: a contract test pinning a cross-file pointer or a removed dependency on an outside plugin is the accepted exception, and the behavior proof stays with strap-skills.
Or drop the removed-text assertions (`superpowers`, `human partner`) and keep the tests that pin a positive route (`harness:strap-debugging` named in the rule, the scoping sentences present).

minor.name: Test-command detector misses common launcher forms and tilde fences
minor.summary:
_TEST_COMMAND only recognizes runs starting at column 0 (after strip) or after '$ ' with the literal spellings npm test / pytest / python -m pytest / cargo test / go test. Bare suite runs written as `python3 -m pytest -q`, `uv run pytest`, `npx vitest run`, or the project's own launcher form `sh "<plugin>/scripts/hpy" -m pytest -q` are never classified as test runs, so they escape the bare-run check. _fenced also toggles only on ``` and ignores ~~~ fences, so any run inside a ~~~bash block is never inspected.

Attack: Add a fenced ```bash block with the line `sh "<plugin>/scripts/hpy" -m pytest -q` (or `python3 -m pytest -q`, `uv run pytest`), or a ~~~bash block with `pytest -q`, to plugins/harness/skills/tdd-strapped/SKILL.md; `python -m pytest tests/skills/test_tdd_strapped_skill_contract.py -q` still passes. The probe at docs/_scratch/pr_review/0337/pr337_20261124T062651Z/probes/probe_regex.py prints cmd=False for each of these lines, so they never reach the bare-run assertion.
fix: Broaden _TEST_COMMAND to match `-m pytest` and `pytest` anywhere on the line (e.g. r"(?:\bpython\d*(?:\.\d+)?\s+-m\s+pytest|\bpytest|\bnpm test|\bnpx (?:jest|vitest)|\bcargo test|\bgo test)\b") and make _fenced toggle on lines starting with ``` or ~~~.

minor.name: tdd-strapped checklist demands a test for every new function; its own reference says trivial code earns none
minor.summary: SKILL.md:330 makes 'Every new function/method has a test' a box, and :340 says an unchecked box means 'You skipped TDD. Start over.' The linked reference writing-good-tests.md:60-63 says constructors, getters, constants and trivial forwarding earn tests only when they validate, normalize, default, derive, enforce or cause side effects, and :153-155 says trivial code earns none and a test written to satisfy process costs maintenance forever. An agent that follows the binding checklist writes the change-detector tests the reference forbids; one that follows the reference fails the checklist and is told to start over.
fix: Reword SKILL.md:330 to 'Every new function/method that validates, normalizes, defaults, derives, enforces or causes a side effect has a test; trivial code is covered through the first consumer-visible result that depends on it' (the wording of writing-good-tests.md:60-63).

minor.name: Shipped test rules condemn the PR's own skill contract tests
minor.summary:
writing-good-tests.md:47-52 says asserting that a skill 'contains an exact line proves only that the source is the source' and that agent documents are tested through the consuming agent's behavior (harness:strap-skills). Its Warning Signs list, line 193, names 'The test greps source text, or asserts a removed symbol stays removed'. An agent following the skill will flag or rewrite the repo's own guard tests, and an agent following repo convention will ignore the skill.
